doc.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Against the Real Book; Odessa jazz party
summary: Criticism of the Real Book and a story of playing with Bob Haggart, Milt Hinton and others in Odessa.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well it’s so funny. As stubborn as a mule and it just drove me up the wall. But the thing that I’m appreciative of is the fact that you watch kids, you watch these kids today. And they get that damn Real Book out and they open the Real Book up and they say okay “Body and Soul” page 6, and they’re all sitting there with music stands and it makes me want to puke. That’s the best word I can use. It’s like get rid of the damn book. You should have these songs in your head. And that was — at least the best thing is that I know them from up here and I can fake them from up here. If somebody called a song I didn’t know I can sit down and I can hear where we’re going because I’m aware of — I was on a bandstand with Bob Haggart and Ralph Sutton and looking up at Bob saying “You’re going to help me out here,” and Bob saying, “don’t worry.” He just looked at me like, and he’d go boom and he’d just look at me.

And he’d just hit them all. And you’d go oh, there they are. And you’d know if it was a D minor chord you’d hear D minor, and then you’d hear down the line D minor, C and you’d hear it all going. And you’d just sit there and he’d go, “you got it?” And he would look at me like you got it. And I’d go oh, okay. And I was so happy that he was being nice to me. And so, that was in Odessa in 1981 I think. Herb Ellis couldn’t make it and my father says, “we’ll take the kid, we’ll take him down there.” And so I found myself on these bandstands with all these guys. Milt Hinton and with Bob Haggart playing rhythm behind Bob Wilber, Carl Fontana or whoever the guys were. And there’s — with the sticks — Cliff Lehman walking around with metal sticks all day. And then Red Norvo was there and I mean it was an amazing group of guys. Just shaking your head. Yank Lawson. And Scott Hamilton and Warren Vache were the new kids on the block then.
